text: hello faithfuls! have you read your bible today? what book are you currently reading? can't wait to get into the Word and spend some quiet time with Jesus 🍵💌

To all my brothers and sisters in Christ: 

Just curious here, but what does your quiet time with Jesus look like? Also how do you stay spiritually disciplined with reading the word and praying?

The older I get, I understand why Jesus 
often withdrew to quiet places.

My baby loves Jesus. Every time I start my devotion, he wakes up and cries. At first, I wondered why. why not just stop and calm him? But then I realized… why not bring him with me instead?

So now, instead of choosing between devotion and comforting my baby, I choose both. Together, we dedicate our time to Him. In those quiet moments, holding my baby while seeking Jesus, my heart feels so full.

Noise is cheap. Quiet strength is forged. 🛡️
​A man who can’t sit in quiet with God will eventually get broken by the noise of the world.
​Look at Jesus in Mark 1:35—before the crowds gathered and demands hit, He pulled away into an isolated place to pray. He made quietness His starting line.
​"In quietness and confident trust is your strength." — Isaiah 30:15
​Win the war for your mind in the morning before the world gets a say.

Sometimes I think we put too much pressure on our quiet time with God.

It doesn’t always have to be an hour-long Bible study or pages of journaling.

Sometimes it’s a few verses, an honest prayer, and a quiet moment with Him. 🤍

What does your quiet time with God look like lately? 🌿
Do you need someone to be in your inbox every day nudging you to spend a little time with Jesus? It’s not a checklist, just 5 days of short messages to spice up your quiet time.
Why nobody told me that growing a closer relationship with God will have you sitting quiet all day not talking to nobody else but Him😭😭😭

The closer we draw to Jesus, the more His peace begins to quiet the noise within us. His presence doesn't always remove every fear, but it reminds us that we never have to face them alone. There is rest, strength, and hope in simply being with Him.

If this sounds like you, follow me. Let’s build that kind of community together. ▓▓

Every morning, I try to spend quiet time with God while having coffee. Hindi madali—ang daming distractions. But I prayed for strength, and He reminded me:
“In the morning, Lord, you hear my voice…” (Psalm 5:3) 🌅

One day, my son Daniel asked if he could read the Bible with me. Dun ko na-realize—our little habits matter. Kids are watching. 🌱💖

Moms, kahit ilang minuto lang sa umaga, choose to talk to God first. Those little eyes will one day thank you. 🙏💙

Maybe the reason quiet time feels hard isn't because you don't love God.
Maybe you've been carrying expectations Jesus never placed on you.
Start simple.
One verse.
One prayer.
One moment.
That's still worship.
Give yourself some grace my girl.
A quiet morning with God can reset your entire mindset before the world even starts talking.
What a blessing to be here again, in the quiet of the Adoration Chapel spending some time alone with Jesus!

If anyone who is a strong believer in Jesus Christ is listening/ happens to come across this post, if you wouldn’t mind praying a small, quiet prayer for me? I’m just feeling frustrated and very discouraged. I’d really appreciate it.🙏🏾
Kneeling at the altar this morning. No performance. No pressure. Just quiet time with Jesus. This is where I remember who I am and whose I am. Everything else can wait.

Partial obedience is still disobedience. Let’s honor God with willing, wholehearted obedience. ❤️

Obedience to God is not dependent on your spouse’s behavior. Scripture never says, “Honor, love, forgive, or serve only if they deserve it.” It calls us to obey the Lord regardless of what others choose.

Your spouse is accountable to God for their obedience, and you are accountable for yours. Don’t let someone else’s disobedience become the excuse for your own.

Sometimes obedience to God costs comfort rather than producing it.
Obedience to God doesn't always lead to the easiest path, but it always leads to the right one.

Read this today: “Love makes obedience to God a desire instead of a burden.”

So true.

Obedience to God is not a one time emotional decision, it is a daily surrender. Every day, we must choose between the broad road of comfort, pleasure, pride, fear, and compromise, or the narrow road of prayer, holiness, humility, sacrifice, love, and truth. Jesus never called us to admire him from a distance. He called us to deny ourselves, take up our cross daily, and follow him, even when obedience is painful, unpopular, or costly.
